protocol: Transfer check, not a pre-registered anchor experiment: this clip was already used for the held-out location QA in 5.14. These state questions were written from visual inspection of sampled frames (3 s contact sheet plus full frames at 10, 20, 30 and 40 s) before the first state-path run on this clip. Labels were not produced by the query detector. The room contains a shelving unit with a kettle and a coffee maker, so 'no kettle on the table' is a place-qualified absence, not a claim that no kettle exists in the room.

questions.query: Is there a plate on the table?
questions.human_evidence: Four white plates with sandwiches/chips are on the wooden dining table at 20 s.

questions.query: Is there a cup on the table?
questions.human_evidence: Four red/pink drink cups are visible on the table at 20 s.

questions.query: Is there a laptop on the table?
questions.human_evidence: No laptop on the table or in the room in any sampled frame.

questions.query: Is there a hammer on the table?
questions.human_evidence: No hammer in any sampled frame.

questions.query: Is there a fork on the table?
questions.human_evidence: No utensils are visible; the food is eaten by hand. This is a detector-hard absence because forks are thin and cluttered.

questions.query: Is there a bottle on the table?
questions.human_evidence: Only red/pink drink cups are on the table; there is no bottle.

questions.query: Is the plate still on the table?
questions.human_evidence: Multiple plates with food remain on the table at 40 s.

questions.query: Is the cup still on the table?
questions.human_evidence: At least one red drink cup sits on the table at 40 s; another is held by a person.
Plates are used in place on the table; at the support level they do not move to another surface.
